thesis: TSMC is the world's dominant pure-play semiconductor foundry, manufacturing the leading-edge chips that power the entire AI buildout — including NVIDIA GPUs, AMD accelerators, Apple silicon, and hyperscaler custom ASICs. With >60% global foundry share and a near-monopoly on advanced (3nm/2nm) nodes and CoWoS advanced packaging, TSMC is the indispensable chokepoint of AI compute. FY2025 revenue of ~$118B (+34% YoY) with ~59% gross margins reflects surging high-performance-computing demand. At ~$392 (ADR) and ~43x trailing / ~33x forward earnings, the premium is supported by pricing power, an unmatched technology lead, and structurally rising AI capex; the dominant offset is concentrated geopolitical (Taiwan/China) risk.

drivers: AI/HPC demand keeps 3nm and 2nm nodes sold out; N2 ramp in 2026 commands premium pricing and lifts blended ASPs
CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity doubles again, easing the AI accelerator bottleneck and capturing more value per wafer
Gross margins expand toward 60%+ on node mix, utilization, and pricing power despite overseas fab cost drag
Arizona and Japan fabs de-risk the geopolitical discount, prompting a multiple re-rating toward global mega-cap tech peers

base_case.assumptions: HPC/AI revenue continues to grow 30%+ and becomes the largest segment; gross margins hold in the high-50s%; capex stays elevated (~$40B/yr); FY2026 revenue grows ~25% with ADR EPS of ~$11–12; the stock trades at ~30–33x forward earnings, roughly in line with the analyst consensus average target near $537.

risks: A cross-strait (Taiwan/China) crisis or blockade disrupts production at the world's most critical fabs
AI capex cycle peaks and hyperscaler/GPU order rates decelerate sharply, driving foundry underutilization
Overseas fab expansion (Arizona, Japan, Germany) dilutes gross margins by several points and pressures returns
Rising competition from Intel Foundry and a resurgent Samsung erodes leading-edge pricing power
The multiple compresses to ~20x on cyclical normalization or a broad AI-trade unwind

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings — HPC/AI revenue mix, N2 ramp progress, and full-year guidance update
N2 (2nm) high-volume production ramp and 2027 capex guidance
Q4 2026 earnings and full-year 2027 outlook, including CoWoS capacity expansion targets
Monthly revenue disclosures — high-frequency read on AI/foundry demand

key_risks: Geopolitical concentration: the vast majority of leading-edge capacity is in Taiwan; a cross-strait conflict would be catastrophic for global supply and the stock
Cyclicality: foundry demand is tied to the AI/semiconductor capex cycle, which could decelerate sharply if AI ROI disappoints
Customer concentration: a handful of clients (Apple, NVIDIA, AMD, and hyperscaler ASIC programs) drive a large share of leading-edge revenue
Margin dilution from overseas fabs (Arizona, Japan, Germany), which carry higher costs than Taiwan operations
Competition from Intel Foundry Services and Samsung at advanced nodes, plus potential customer in-sourcing
Currency and export-control exposure: NT dollar swings and U.S./China chip restrictions can affect reported results and end demand
